title: Deformation and differential calculus for a logarithmically smooth chart
statement:
Let $f:(X,M)\to(Y,N)$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] that is log smooth in the chart sense of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Define the relative logarithmic differential sheaf $\omega_f$ as the sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules generated locally by $da$ for local functions $a$ and $d\log m$ for local log sections $m$, with relations: $d$ is additive, $d(ab)=a\,db+b\,da$, $dc=0$ for functions from $Y$, $d\log(mm')=d\log m+d\log m'$, $d\alpha(m)=\alpha(m)d\log m$, and $d\log f^\flat(n)=0$ for sections $n$ of $N$.

Then the underlying scheme map is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and $\omega_f$ is finite locally free: etale locally it is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X^s$ for some finite $s$. These assertions and the following lifting statements are preserved by etale localization on $X$ and $Y$ [def-weil-etale-morphism].

Let $(T_0,L_0)\hookrightarrow(T,L)$ be a first order thickening of fine log schemes over $(Y,N)$, meaning a closed immersion of underlying schemes with square-zero ideal $\mathcal I$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], with fine log structures. Here $T$ is an arbitrary scheme, not necessarily locally Noetherian, and a log structure on it means, as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] but without that hypothesis, a sheaf of commutative monoids $L$ on the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] with a homomorphism $\alpha:L\to(\mathcal O_T,\cdot)$ inducing an isomorphism $\alpha^{-1}(\mathcal O_T^\times)\simeq\mathcal O_T^\times$; it is fine if etale locally it has a chart by a finitely generated integral commutative monoid $P$, meaning that at each geometric point $\bar t$, with $A=\mathcal O_{T,\bar t}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and $\beta:P\to A$ the composite with $\alpha$, the induced map $P\oplus_{\beta^{-1}(A^\times)}A^\times\to L_{\bar t}$ is an isomorphism; log morphisms are defined as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Require it to be strict: on each geometric stalk its log structure is the pushout of $L$ and $\mathcal O_{T_0}^{\times}$ over $\mathcal O_T^{\times}$. For every log morphism $a_0:(T_0,L_0)\to(X,M)$ over $(Y,N)$, a lift $a:(T,L)\to(X,M)$ exists etale locally on $T$.

On any open of $T$ with one such lift, all lifts form a torsor under relative log derivations. Explicitly a log derivation with values in $\mathcal I$, with scalars acting through $a_0$, is a pair $(D,\delta)$: $D:a_0^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal I$ is additive, vanishes on functions from $Y$, and satisfies $D(ab)=a_0^*(a)D(b)+a_0^*(b)D(a)$; $\delta:a_0^{-1}M^{\rm gp}\to\mathcal I$ is an additive homomorphism vanishing on $f^\flat N^{\rm gp}$, with $D(\alpha(m))=a_0^*(\alpha(m))\delta(m)$. Such pairs are exactly the $\mathcal O$-linear maps from the pullback of $\omega_f$ to $\mathcal I$, by $da\mapsto D(a)$ and $d\log m\mapsto\delta(m)$. Here the pullback means tensoring $a_0^{-1}\omega_f$ with $\mathcal O_{T_0}$ over $a_0^{-1}\mathcal O_X$. Acting by $(D,\delta)$ replaces a lift's ring map $a^\sharp(b)$ by $a^\sharp(b)+D(b)$ and its log map $a^\flat(m)$ by $a^\flat(m)(1+\delta(m))$. Every pair of lifts is related in this way by a unique log derivation. The ideal is an $\mathcal O_{T_0}$-module since $\mathcal I^2=0$, and $1+\mathcal I$ is identified with its additive group by $v\mapsto1+v$.

proof.text: Choose compatible charts $P\to Q$ on $V\to B$ from the chart definition, and put $W=B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$. The finite-presentation theorem for commutative monoids gives generators $q_1,\ldots,q_r$ and finitely many relations $a_j=b_j$ for $Q$, hence $\mathbf Z[Q]=\mathbf Z[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x^{a_j}-x^{b_j})$. If $p_1,\ldots,p_t$ generate $P$, choose monomials $x^{v_k}$ representing their images. As a $\mathbf Z[P]$-algebra this presentation adds just the equations $z^{p_k}=x^{v_k}$; they imply compatibility for all of $P$. Thus $\mathbf Z[P]\to\mathbf Z[Q]$ is finitely presented. Over an affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset B$, the affine fibre-product formula identifies $W$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q])$. Finite presentation is preserved by this scalar extension, so $W\to B$ is locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence, monoid presentation consequence via the cited node; finite-presentation scalar extension and affine fibre product as in the cited statements.

proof.text: The comparison $c:V\to W$ is smooth and therefore locally of finite presentation by the smoothness definition. The etale map $B\to Y$ is locally of finite presentation. Composition with $W\to B$ shows $V\to Y$ is locally of finite presentation. The etale maps $V\to X$ cover $X$, are flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply fppf source locality to this family: $f:X\to Y$ is locally of finite presentation. This requires no quasi-compact cover and also covers $X=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 02H6, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth; descent of local finite presentation through the cited fppf-source-locality statement.

proof.text: Reduce a strict test square etale locally on $T$ to these charts. Pull back a chart neighbourhood $V\to X$ along $a_0$; its projection to $T_0$ is etale, and these projections cover $T_0$. Thickening invariance lifts this etale cover to $T$. On affine opens of the lifted cover, the map $T_0\to B$ extends uniquely to a scheme map $T\to B$ over $Y$: $B\to Y$ is etale, hence flat and unramified. Its log map is specified by the already fixed log map to $Y$: locally choose a chart for $N$, pull its sections to $L$, and use the associated-log universal property for the pulled-back log structure on $B$. This is compatible with the ring map because $T\to B$ is over $Y$. Its reduction is the given base log map, by uniqueness on that chart. We now have a square over $(B,N_B)$ with $a_0:T_0\to V$ and a fixed monoid chart $P\to Q$.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, chart setup, pp.136--138; agent expansion of the etale-local reduction, using Stacks Tag 03SI and the cited formal-etale lemma.

proof.text: At a corresponding geometric point of $T_0$ and $T$, write $J=\mathcal I_{\bar t}$, $E=L_{\bar t}^{\rm gp}$ and $E_0=L_{0,\bar t}^{\rm gp}$. Choose a fine chart of $L$ near this point. Strictness identifies $L_0$ with its reduced associated log structure, so the chart-thickening theorem says every fibre $L_{\bar t}\to L_{0,\bar t}$ is a nonempty free $1+J$-torsor. Consequently $E\to E_0$ is surjective with kernel $1+J$: if $m/n$ reduces to $1$, their reductions agree and $m=n(1+v)$ for a unique $v\in J$. Moreover $L_{\bar t}=E\times_{E_0}L_{0,\bar t}$: if $e$ reduces to $m_0$, choose $m$ above $m_0$, and $e/m\in1+J$, hence $e\in L_{\bar t}$. Integrality permits these embeddings in the group completions. Finally $(1+v)(1+w)=1+(v+w)$ since $J^2=0$. This gives the exact abelian-group sequence $0\to(J,+)\to E\to E_0\to0$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1, p.69, associated-log conventions; explicit elementary group-completion calculation from the cited strict chart-thickening statement.

proof.text: The base log map and $a_0$ give compatible homomorphisms $a:P^{\rm gp}\to E$ and $b_0:Q^{\rm gp}\to E_0$ with $\pi a=b_0u$. Group completions are finitely generated: the finite monoid generators also generate the groups. By the chart hypothesis $K=\ker u$ and $C_{\rm tors}$, for $C=\operatorname{coker}u$, are finite of invertible orders near the image in $V$. Their orders are units on $T_0$ and then on $T$: if $rs=1+v$ with $v\in J$, multiply $s$ by $1-v$ to obtain an inverse to $r$. Thus multiplication by both orders is an automorphism on the module $J$. The compatible abelian-group lifting lemma gives $h:Q^{\rm gp}\to E$ with $hu=a$ and $\pi h=b_0$. Since $b_0(Q)$ lies in $L_{0,\bar t}$, the cartesian description in step 4 gives $h(Q)\subset L_{\bar t}$. We have therefore lifted the monoid map compatibly with $P$, without having assumed a scheme map $T\to W$.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, p.252, invokes Kato Theorem 3.5; agent-formulated forward chart-lifting argument, with its arithmetic isolated in the cited lemma.

proof.text: Spread this stalk map to an etale neighbourhood of $\bar t$. Represent the images of the finitely many $Q$-generators by local sections of $L$. Impose the finitely many relations of $Q$, compatibility on generators of $P$, and the finitely many reduction equalities to $a_0$. Each equality of germs holds after a pointed neighbourhood refinement, and cofilteredness gives a common refinement for the finite list. Thus $h:Q\to\Gamma(T,L)$ exists locally with exactly the required compatibility and reduction. Its structure functions give $\mathbf Z[Q]\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. Together with $T\to B$ this defines a scheme map $T\to W$, reducing to $ca_0$, by the affine-spectrum and fibre-product universal properties. Pass to affine opens of $T$ and apply the formal smoothness of $c:V\to W$ to obtain a scheme lift $a:T\to V$ over $W$. The associated-log universal property gives its unique log map prescribed by $h$, since the $Q$-functions of $a$ are exactly $\alpha_Lh(q)$. Compatibility on $P$ makes this a log lift over $B$, and its reduction agrees with $a_0$ on both functions and log sections. This proves etale-local existence for every fine strict test, with no Noetherian assumption on $T$.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2 and XVI Proposition 3.6.3, chart route; agent expansion of forward Kato chart lifting. Ordinary smooth lifting is Stacks Tag 02H6, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth.

proof.text: The lifting property just proved persists under any compatible etale localization $e:X'\to X$, $d:Y'\to Y$ with pulled-back log structures. Given a test for $X'\to Y'$, first lift its composite to $X\to Y$ by step 6. Locally on affine $T$ lift $T_0\to X'$ uniquely over that map to $X$, using formal etaleness of $e$. The two resulting maps $T\to Y'$ over $Y$ agree on $T_0$, so uniqueness for the etale map $d$ makes them equal. Log maps on pulled-back structures are forced by the associated-log universal property. Thus this is a log lift over the specified $Y'$, not just over $Y$. The proof works with either localization the identity and needs no Noetherian test scheme.

proof.text: Apply the logarithmic differential calculus from strict infinitesimal lifting to $f$. Its hypotheses are now verified: $X,Y$ are locally Noetherian fs, the underlying map is locally of finite presentation by steps 1--2, arbitrary fine strict first-order tests lift by steps 3--6, and this property persists under compatible etale localization by step 7. Its sheaf presentation has precisely the generators and relations defining $\omega_f$ in the statement, so it is the same sheaf. The cited statement yields etale-local finite freeness of $\omega_f$. It also supplies the stated sheaf of lifts and its action by relative log derivations. No converse chart criterion or the parent infinitesimal-criterion node is used.

proof.text: For clarity the torsor formulas can also be read directly from the relations. An $\mathcal O_{T_0}$-linear map $a_0^*\omega_f\to\mathcal I$ sends $db$ and $d\log m$ to $D(b)$ and $\delta(m)$; the defining relations are exactly additivity, Leibniz, base vanishing, and $D(\alpha(m))=a_0^*\alpha(m)\delta(m)$. Conversely these identities define such a map, uniquely on generators. As $\mathcal I^2=0$, the formulas $a'^\sharp(b)=a^\sharp(b)+D(b)$ and $a'^\flat(m)=a^\flat(m)(1+\delta(m))$ preserve multiplication. In particular $\alpha(a'^\flat(m))=a^\sharp\alpha(m)+a_0^*\alpha(m)\delta(m)=a'^\sharp\alpha(m)$. Thus they give the claimed action. For two lifts their difference on functions is $D$, and the unique unit ratio in each log-section fibre is $1+\delta(m)$ by the strict-thickening statement. These differences satisfy the same identities, and their uniqueness proves freeness and transitivity on any open admitting a lift.

proof.text: For compatible etale localizations $e:X'\to X$ and $d:Y'\to Y$, set $Z=X\times_Y Y'$. Both $Z\to X$ and $X'\to X$ are etale, the first by etale base change. The induced map $X'\to Z$ is therefore etale by composition cancellation. Over affine opens, the cited affine fibre-product formula and finite-presentation scalar extension show $Z\to Y'$ is locally of finite presentation. Composing with $X'\to Z$ gives this property for $f':X'\to Y'$. Etale localizations remain locally Noetherian: their affine coordinate rings are finitely presented, hence finite type, over Noetherian rings, and the cited Noetherian finite-type theorem applies. Their pulled-back log structures are fs by the same etale-local chart definition. Step 7 gives all the strict-test lifting hypotheses for $f'$, including their further etale localization. Apply the existing lifting-differential calculus to $f'$ to obtain finite freeness and its torsor statements. The calculations in step 9 use only restriction of functions, log sections and the square-zero ideal, so give precisely the same action formulas after localization.
